analysis.title: Nasdaq 9% Off Its High, Euro Gas Through €100: Goldman's Last "Source Of Calm" Is Central Banks... "Good Luck"
key_insights: Goldman FICC (Rikin Shah, Cosimo Codacci-Pisanelli) 'Risk Jitters' Macro Roadmap: rates are stuck between an AI-driven equity drawdown and an energy shock. The recent source of calm is central banks trying to reduce volatility. Goldman says the market is not in a stable equilibrium and that rates can re-price significantly if one driver flips.

Friday Oct 30 tape: Intel fell the most on record, the Nasdaq 100 closed down roughly 3.5% (it was down 2.8% at the open), Brent touched $118 (a six-month high) and the 10Y yield fell to a six-week low below 4.9%. That is stocks down, oil up, yields down.

The Fed held this week on a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. The ECB also held. Goldman reads both as being on a quarterly hiking path that skipped this week. December remains live, and the pause buys time to assess risk.

Six weeks ago October priced 18bp of ECB hikes at one point and the Fed's October meeting priced 17bp. Since then Brent is up $9/bbl and TTF up €16/MWh since mid-September, and the market prices 4.5% euro-area headline inflation by Q1. The September US core print was 'unambiguously strong' per Shah.

The central banks paused because the Nasdaq 100 fell nearly 9% from its early-October high, US HY CDX widened 20bp and OAT/Bund widened about 60bp. Goldman says this feeds the central banks' reaction function.

Goldman's US financial conditions index has tightened about 35bp this year, almost all from long-end rates and the dollar, while equities and credit are still a net easing year-to-date. Europe is broadly flat, as a weaker euro offsets rates, sovereign spreads and stocks. Goldman says the direction of the tail matters more than the level of the index.

Rates correlations have flipped. In October the correlation of daily 10Y UST moves with NDX is +0.60 and with Brent is -0.28, so equities are now the primary driver of US rates. This is why 10Y USTs rallied in October despite higher oil.

European rates are less clear. October correlations of 10Y EUR swaps to the Nasdaq, Brent and TTF are all close to zero, and 1-month realized vol on 10Y EUR swaps is 57bp annualized. Goldman says implied vol trades at a premium because of the unstable equilibrium.

Goldman's rates scenario map: de-escalation plus continued equity cracks drives a sustained rate rally. Equities rebounding on AI resilience with energy still elevated drives the next leg higher in yields. Until the drivers line up, European rates are pulled both ways and US rates trade off equities.

Goldman's credit desk described client sentiment on Friday as 'a crisis without a crisis'. Goldman's Mark Wilson separately argued in his weekly note that reports of the AI capex demise and funding threat are greatly exaggerated, while admitting it had been a bruising couple of weeks.

European natgas (TTF) broke through €100/MWh this week, 36% above the end-September close, on post-midterm re-escalation headlines. Hormuz LNG exports have dipped back to 20-25% of pre-war levels versus the 65% by January that GIR's base case needs.
NW European gas storage is at its lowest level in 14 years, 64% full against a pre-2022 average of 88%, and forecasts have turned colder with withdrawals picking up.

GIR TTF scenarios: Hormuz supply recovers, base case about €70. Low Hormuz flows with normal weather, about €105 to force LNG demand destruction elsewhere. Cold winter with subdued Strait flows, about €150. The March 2027 contract is at about €98, so Shah says there is less asymmetry for TTF longs than a month ago (when TTF sat on the base case at 72) but still scope for a convex move higher.
Iran conducted its first limpet mine attack on a tanker since 2019, and the WSJ reports the US told Gulf states to prepare for 'a short, intense campaign' after Tuesday's vote.

UK: Wednesday's budget was low-volatility, with headroom against the deficit rule falling to £15bn from £24bn, in line with consensus. Hard decisions (departmental cuts, health, defence at 3% of GDP by 2030) were pushed to next year's Spending Review. Goldman sees further term premium reduction for gilts, helped by a collapse in net duration supply, and UK risk spreads are near six-year lows per Bloomberg's Simon White.

Bank of England next week: a hike is nearly fully priced (24bp) and the market prices a 40% chance of a follow-up hike in December. The BoE curve prices roughly 110bp of cumulative hikes into late 2027 versus roughly 65bp for both the Fed and ECB. Goldman's base case is that the reluctant hikers follow the Fed and ECB's quarterly pace, and a clear quarterly signal would take some premium out of the UK front end.
Goldman's asset allocators recently shifted to overweight 10Y government bonds.

Author view (Zero Hedge, not Goldman): oil is more likely than AI to flip first, which would turn the central banks' calm into volatility, since a Fed and ECB with 4.5% euro-area inflation priced and December live cannot stay on the sidelines.
ECB President Lagarde is heading for the exit in February (described as an early exit announced this week), creating a succession issue for the ECB.
